# Formation v37 binary outer-coinvariant collapse -- Forge handoff

For a finite nonabelian simple species `T`, let `A=Hom(M(T),Q/Z)` and let the full image of `Out(T)` act on `A`. Formation Polarization v37 proves that the outer coinvariant `A_Out(T)` is either trivial or `C2`. Every odd-primary coinvariant vanishes, and the 2-primary coinvariant has exponent at most two and is cyclic.

For the full-outer finite-simple compiler this deletes the higher p-adic phase tower, odd-prime projective atoms, and positive cancellation tethers from the live state space. A mixed copy-minimal critical packet can only be binary and its global code is the unique full-support line `<(1,...,1)>` in `F2^r`. The one-witness Schur-section machinery of v36 remains available for restricted outer actions and broader perfect/quasisimple palettes but is not needed for this normalized finite-simple branch.

Forge treats this as a scope reduction, not as a retraction of v33-v36.
